[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Toothpicks of equal length are used to build a rectangular grid as shown. If the grid is \(20\) toothpicks high and \(10\) toothpicks wide, then the number of toothpicks used is

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(\angle A=100^\circ,\) \(\angle B=50^\circ,\) \(\angle C=30^\circ,\) \(AH\) is an altitude, and \(BM\) is a median. Then \(\angle MHC=\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Two strips of width \(1\) overlap at an angle of \(\alpha\) as shown. The area of the overlap (shown shaded) is

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB=5,\) \(BC=7,\) \(AC=9\) and \(D\) is on \(\overline{AC}\) with \(BD=5.\) Find the ratio \(AD:DC.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A square flag has a red cross of uniform width with a blue square in the center on a white background as shown. (The cross is symmetric with respect to each of the diagonals of the square.) If the entire cross (both the red arms and the blue center) takes up \(36\%\) of the area of the flag, what percent of the area of the flag is blue?

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A particle moves through the first quadrant as follows. During the first minute it moves from the origin to \((1,0).\) Thereafter, it continues to follow the directions indicated in the figure, going back and forth between the positive \(x\) and \(y\) axes, moving one unit of distance parallel to an axis in each minute. At which point will the particle be after exactly \(1989\) minutes?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

If the markings on the number line shown are equally spaced, what is the number \(y?\)

mappings.answerReason: The perpendicular projections of A and B leave equal overhangs of (10-4)/2=3. Thus B's foot is 7 units from D. Since B is the midpoint of DE, its horizontal coordinate is half that of E, giving DF=14 and CF=14-10=4.

mappings.answerReason: There are 21 horizontal rows of 10 toothpicks and 11 vertical columns of 20 toothpicks. The total is 21×10+11×20=430.

mappings.rationale: The median makes M the midpoint of AC, which is the hypotenuse of right triangle AHC. The hypotenuse-midpoint property gives HM=MC, allowing an isosceles-triangle angle calculation.
mappings.answerReason: In right triangle AHC, HM=AM=MC. Hence triangle HMC is isosceles, so ∠MHC=∠MCH=∠ACB=30°.

mappings.rationale: The overlap is a parallelogram with altitude 1. A right-triangle sine ratio relates its base to the other strip's perpendicular width. For the depicted obtuse angle, its acute supplement has the same sine.
mappings.answerReason: If b is the horizontal base of the overlap, the perpendicular distance between the slanted boundaries is b sin(α)=1. Therefore its area is b×1=1/sin(α).

mappings.rationale: The equal lengths AB=BD place B on the perpendicular bisector of AD. The three given side lengths determine the two subsegment lengths, whose ratio is simplified. A cosine-law calculation is another useful route.
mappings.answerReason: Let H be B's perpendicular projection onto AC and AH=x. Subtracting squared-distance equations gives 49-25=(9-x)²-x², so x=19/6. Since H bisects AD, AD=19/3 and DC=9-19/3=8/3. Thus AD:DC=19:8.
